::: {#sol-write-in-matrix-form}

Read the coefficients straight off the rule.
There are three inputs, so $p = 3$:

$$\vec w = \begin{bmatrix} 0.4 \\ 0.2 \\ 1.5 \end{bmatrix},
\qquad b = -30$$

and the rule is $f(\vx) = \vec w\' \vx + b$.
For the patient,

$$\vx = \begin{bmatrix} 50 \\ 130 \\ 28 \end{bmatrix}$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
\vec w\' \vx
&= (0.4)(50) + (0.2)(130) + (1.5)(28) \\
&= 20 + 26 + 42 \\
&= 88
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(\vx)
&= 88 - 30 \\
&= 58
\end{aligned}
$$

Two things are worth noticing.
The coefficients are not comparable as they stand: $1.5$ is the largest
number but BMI is measured on the smallest scale,
so the weight on a feature says nothing on its own about how much that
feature matters.
And $b = -30$ is doing real work --- without it the score would be $88$,
which is a different clinical claim entirely.

:::
